To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

AS160 is phosphorylated in human adipose tissue of lean and obese patients, and that AS160 phosphorylation associates with the insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in human adipose cells and with insulin resistance in adipose tissue in obese patients.

AS160 is a key regulator of insulin-stimulated glucose uptake and that AS160 and SGK phosphorylation are altered in obese patients with type 2 diabetes and that these alterations associate with impaired insulin signaling in the skeletal muscle and adipose tissue.

(1) the basal phosphorylation status of AS160 and SGK in adipose tissue is associated with impaired incretin secretion and type 2 (T2) diabetes in obese patients; (2) in obese individuals, the phosphorylation status of both AS160 and SGKK is associated with insulin sensitivity; and (3) in obese individuals and in mice with obesity, the phosphorylation of AS160 and/or SGKK is associated to the phosphorylation of Akt and GSK-3β
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the protein kinase B (PKB) and the AS160 protein in insulin action.
the identification and characterization of the molecular mechanisms that control insulin-stimulated translocation of the insulin-responsive glucose transporter GLUT4 in adipocytes.
the identification of a novel molecular link between the insulin signaling and incretin signaling pathways.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
obesity, diabetes and insulin resistance are associated with an increased expression and/or activity of the serine/threonine kinase Akt, which is the key regulator of insulin action.

the results of this study suggest that the low AS160 phosphorylation in adipose tissue from obese subjects is associated with a decreased insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in the adipose tissue and a reduced insulin sensitivity of the whole body.

the results of this study suggest that the presence of a high level of AS160 basal phosphorylation and a low level of AS160 phosphorylation in response to insulin is associated with impaired insulin sensitivity and glucose tolerance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AS160-SGK axis is a potential therapeutic target to improve incretin secretion and glycemia in obesity.
the AS160 and SGK phosphorylation state in adipose tissue is linked to the development of type 2 diabetes.

this study demonstrates that the low basal phosphorylation state of AS160 and high basal phosphorylation of SGK are linked to the development of type 2 diabetes and the impairment of incretin profile in adipose tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AS160 is an important regulator of insulin-stimulated glucose uptake in adipose tissue and skeletal muscle.
the AS160 protein is a potential therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes.
the AS160/Sgk axis is a key player in the pathogenesis of insulin resistance in obesity.
